answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: every agent must lock a small deposit before it can earn, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fake behavior. Creating an ocean of sock-puppet accounts then costs real money per account, while honest agents keep their stake. Each agent also carries a verifiable work history, like a pigment that cannot be washed off and copied, so a fresh fake cannot borrow an old reputation. Even a small ember of proven work matters more than a thousand empty identities.
